name: Congenital Hypothyroidism Due to Dyshormonogenesis
aliases: Genetic Hypothyroidism due to Thyroid Hormone Synthesis Defect

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in populations with consanguinity

criteria.description: Elevated serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels in neonatal screening
Low serum free thyroxine (FT4) and triiodothyronine (T3) levels
Normal or enlarged thyroid gland on ultrasound or radionuclide scan indicating dyshormonogenesis rather than agenesis or ectopy
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding thyroid hormone synthesis enzymes (e.g., TPO, TG, DUOX2)
Presence of clinical features consistent with hypothyroidism in neonate or infant

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated TSH with low thyroid hormones plus normal thyroid gland imaging consistent with dyshormonogenesis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory for clinical diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Due to hypothyroidism-induced impaired bilirubin metabolism
Enlarged tongue characteristic of congenital hypothyroidism
Reduced muscle tone in affected infants

common.notes: Common due to slowed gastrointestinal motility
Due to hypotonia and connective tissue laxity

occasional.notes: Due to decreased eccrine gland function
Resulting from laryngeal edema and muscle weakness
Slow heart rate due to hypothyroidism

rare.notes: Reported in some cases due to developmental delay
Due to severe untreated hypothyroidism and metabolic disturbances

laboratory: Low serum free T4 and T3
Normal or elevated radioactive iodine uptake
imaging: Normal or enlarged thyroid gland on ultrasound
Normal or increased uptake on thyroid scintigraphy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in TPO, TG, DUOX2, SLC5A5, or other thyroid hormone synthesis genes
other: Newborn screening programs detect elevated TSH
Response to levothyroxine therapy confirms diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Absent or ectopic thyroid gland on imaging
Low or absent radioactive iodine uptake
Temporary hypothyroidism resolving within weeks to months
Often related to maternal antibodies or iodine exposure
Normal thyroid anatomy and function eventually

redFlags: Signs of thyroid hormone resistance or other endocrine abnormalities
references: Lazar L, et al. Congenital hypothyroidism due to dyshormonogenesis: clinical and molecular aspects. Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2018.
Rose SR, et al. Update of newborn screening and therapy for congenital hypothyroidism. Pediatrics. 2016.
